Synopsis:
|Tieflings joined a random combat and were dragged far from Lae'zel Recruitment. They will leave out of stage while saying this instead of going back to the scene.|

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_AD_LeavingAnyCombat2.json: The lines occur after a chaotic encounter in the Druid Grove where two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) attempted to seize a defiant githyanki, Lae'zel, expecting an easy prisoner but finding far more resistance than they anticipated. Off‑screen there is wreckage and a loud blast (the Nautiloid/ship crash) and general danger that pulls the tieflings away from the recruitment/confrontation area. Rather than returning to tend the prisoner or continue arguing, Damays/Nymessa are abandoning the scene — announcing they "can't remain" and departing — so their spoken exit replaces any further on‑stage action. Other companions (for example Shadowheart) or prior choices may have already shaped loyalties and whether you tried to free, bind, or attack Lae'zel.
- Laezel_Recruitment_InCage.json: |Lae'zel is still in the cage. The tieflings have been dealt with one way or another. She must be freed before she can be recruited.|
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_TieflingsSceneFallback.json: You arrive in the Druid Grove just after the attack on the den, where two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) have trapped an alien-looking githyanki, Lae'zel, in a cage and are arguing over whether to haul her back to their camp or leave her be. The normal spoken exchange has glitched into a telepathic mid‑meld: Lae'zel's lips stay still while her thoughts hit your skull, causing a brief ache and giving you unsettling insight into your condition (the tadpole). The tieflings expected an easy prisoner but Lae'zel is openly defiant and dangerous, so you can intervene (free or neutralize her), side with the tieflings, or let them take her. If Shadowheart is present she will quietly warn you not to trust Lae'zel because of past missions against the gith; celebrations in the grove and an off‑screen blast/ship crash are already drawing attention.
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_PickASide.json: The scene takes place in the Druid Grove just after the attack on the goblin den: the grove has been secured, celebrations are already happening, and Halsin has returned but postponed any talk about the player’s tadpole. A band of tieflings — likely the returning scouts/leaders who picked up command after the fight (Cerys/Asharak may be among them) — have seized Lae'zel and are lowering her toward the grove because the player either urged them to kill her or allowed them to take her. Lae'zel is defiant and issues an ultimatum, and this is the player’s last chance to pick a side: let the tieflings execute her, intervene to protect her, or attack her directly. Companions and nearby NPCs may be present and will react according to prior choices and flags.
- CHA_LaeZelRecruitment_AD_EscortStart.json: Lae'zel, a captured githyanki, has just been shot down from her cage by a band of tieflings who plan to bind her and haul her back to their grove. The tieflings (voices like Damays and Nymessa) are already talking about tying her up and moving her, implying they expect an easy prisoner. Lae'zel, however, is openly defiant and contemptuous, making it clear she will not surrender quietly. The exchange reflects a botched capture: the tieflings misjudged their opponent and didn’t anticipate how resistance-oriented and dangerous she is.

|Lae'zel is still in the cage. The tieflings have been dealt with one way or another. She must be freed before she can be recruited.|

You arrive in the Druid Grove just after the attack on the den, where two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) have trapped an alien-looking githyanki, Lae'zel, in a cage and are arguing over whether to haul her back to their camp or leave her be. The normal spoken exchange has glitched into a telepathic mid‑meld: Lae'zel's lips stay still while her thoughts hit your skull, causing a brief ache and giving you unsettling insight into your condition (the tadpole). The tieflings expected an easy prisoner but Lae'zel is openly defiant and dangerous, so you can intervene (free or neutralize her), side with the tieflings, or let them take her. If Shadowheart is present she will quietly warn you not to trust Lae'zel because of past missions against the gith; celebrations in the grove and an off‑screen blast/ship crash are already drawing attention.

The scene takes place in the Druid Grove just after the attack on the goblin den: the grove has been secured, celebrations are already happening, and Halsin has returned but postponed any talk about the player’s tadpole. A band of tieflings — likely the returning scouts/leaders who picked up command after the fight (Cerys/Asharak may be among them) — have seized Lae'zel and are lowering her toward the grove because the player either urged them to kill her or allowed them to take her. Lae'zel is defiant and issues an ultimatum, and this is the player’s last chance to pick a side: let the tieflings execute her, intervene to protect her, or attack her directly. Companions and nearby NPCs may be present and will react according to prior choices and flags.

Lae'zel, a captured githyanki, has just been shot down from her cage by a band of tieflings who plan to bind her and haul her back to their grove. The tieflings (voices like Damays and Nymessa) are already talking about tying her up and moving her, implying they expect an easy prisoner. Lae'zel, however, is openly defiant and contemptuous, making it clear she will not surrender quietly. The exchange reflects a botched capture: the tieflings misjudged their opponent and didn’t anticipate how resistance-oriented and dangerous she is.
context: Damays and Nymessa are two tieflings who seized a defiant githyanki, Lae'zel, in the Druid Grove expecting an easy prisoner but finding far more resistance than they anticipated. A loud blast and wreckage from the Nautiloid/ship crash and the general danger off‑screen pull them away from the recruitment/confrontation area. Rather than return to tend the captive or continue arguing, they announce they "can't remain" and leave the scene off‑stage — their spoken exit replaces any further on‑stage action. Lae'zel remains caged and must still be freed to be recruited, and other companions or prior choices (for example Shadowheart or Halsin) may already have shaped loyalties and how NPCs react.
